episodes.title: The Transatlantic Slave Trade
episodes.description: Examine the forced transport of captive Africans to the Americas and the brutal conditions of the Middle Passage.

episodes.title: Slavery in the American Colonies
episodes.description: We'll look at the experiences of Anthony Johnson and John Punch to see how legal precedents that greatly influenced the development of slavery were set.

episodes.title: Elizabeth Key
episodes.description: Follow Elizabeth Key’s court battle for freedom and examine how legal challenges could confront slavery in colonial Virginia.

episodes.title: Slave Codes
episodes.description: Today, we'll learn how Colonies put laws in place to restrict the movement and freedoms of enslaved people and free Black people.

episodes.title: The Germantown Petition Against Slavery
episodes.description: Study the 1688 Germantown Petition and its early religious and moral arguments against slavery.

episodes.title: The Stono Rebellion
episodes.description: Explore the Stono Rebellion, broader forms of resistance by enslaved people, and the restrictions used to keep them in bondage.

episodes.title: Phillis Wheatley
episodes.description: Learn how Phillis Wheatley’s poetry challenged white colonists’ assumptions about Black people in colonial America.

episodes.title: The American Revolution
episodes.description: Examine why Black people fought on both sides of the American Revolution despite being excluded from its promises of liberty.

episodes.title: The US Constitution, 3/5, and the Slave Trade Clause
episodes.description: Explore how constitutional compromises, including the Three-Fifths and Fugitive Slave clauses, reinforced slavery despite revolutionary ideals.

episodes.title: The Fugitive Slave Act of 1793
episodes.description: Examine the Fugitive Slave Law of 1793, how enslavers used it, and its lasting effects.

episodes.title: Women’s Experience Under Slavery
episodes.description: Today, Clint Smith teaches you about the experience of enslaved women, and how their experience of slavery was different than men.

episodes.title: The Louisiana Rebellion of 1811
episodes.description: Explore Louisiana’s German Coast Uprising of 1811 and the lasting consequences of this rebellion by enslaved people.

episodes.title: The Rise of Cotton
episodes.description: Today we'll learn about the growth of the cotton industry, who benefitted from it, and who was left out.

episodes.title: Maria Stewart
episodes.description: Clint Smith teaches you about Maria Stewart, a Black woman who lived in the 19th century and was a pioneering abolitionist, writer, and orator.

episodes.title: The Underground Railroad
episodes.description: Trace the Underground Railroad’s origins and the people, routes, and safe houses that helped enslaved people escape.

episodes.title: The Dred Scott Decision
episodes.description: Examine the Dred Scott decision of 1857 and how denying Black citizenship deepened slavery and tensions over abolition.

episodes.title: Frederick Douglass
episodes.description: Clint Smith teaches you about one of the most famous writers, orators, and advocates of the 19th century, Frederick Douglass.

episodes.title: Black Americans in the Civil War
episodes.description: Clint Smith will teach you about how Black people fought and participated in the war, the Emancipation Proclamation, and lots more.

episodes.title: Reconstruction
episodes.description: Today we'll learn about the Reconstruction amendments, the Freedman's Bureau, and the election of 1876, among other things.

episodes.title: Ida B. Wells
episodes.description: In this video, we'll learn about the life story of journalist, orator, teacher, suffragette, and anti-lynching activist Ida B. Wells-Barnett.

episodes.title: Plessy v Ferguson and Segregation
episodes.description: Examine how Plessy v. Ferguson entrenched racial segregation and how the promise of separate but equal accommodations went unfulfilled.

episodes.title: Booker T. Washington and W.E.B. DuBois
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Black American History, Clint Smith compares the competing schools of thought of Booker T. Washington and W.E.B. Dubois.

episodes.title: The Black Women’s Club Movement
episodes.description: Explore how Black women’s clubs organized against racism and misogyny to expand civil and political rights.

episodes.title: The Great Migration
episodes.description: Trace the Great Migration and the opportunities and racial violence that drove Black Americans from the South to other regions.

episodes.title: The Red Summer of 1919
episodes.description: During the Red Summer of 1919 violence against Black people broke out across the United States.

episodes.title: Arts and Letters of the Harlem Renaissance
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Black American History, Clint Smith will teach you about the Harlem Renaissance.

episodes.title: Political Thought in the Harlem Renaissance
episodes.description: Explore political ideas of the Harlem Renaissance, including civil rights, fair labor practices, and Black nationalism.

episodes.title: The Great Depression
episodes.description: Examine how the Great Depression affected Black Americans and exposed the unequal burdens of economic crisis.

episodes.title: The Tuskegee Experiment
episodes.description: Examine the Tuskegee syphilis study, its racist medical abuses, and its enduring impact on trust in healthcare.

episodes.title: Zora Neale Hurston
episodes.description: Explore Zora Neale Hurston’s work as an anthropologist and novelist documenting Black life in the American South.

episodes.title: World War II
episodes.description: Today we'll learn about the experience of Black Americans in World War II.

episodes.title: Randolph, Rustin, and the Origins of the March on Washington
episodes.description: Today we'll learn about Randolph, Bayard Rustin, the march they planned, and the movement it inspired.

episodes.title: School Segregation and Brown v Board
episodes.description: Trace the NAACP’s legal campaign against school segregation, culminating in Brown v. Board of Education.

episodes.title: Emmet Till
episodes.description: In 1955, a 14-year-old boy named Emmett Till was brutally murdered in Money, Mississippi.

episodes.title: The Montgomery Bus Boycott
episodes.description: For 381 days in 1955 and 1956, the Black citizens of Montgomery, Alabama boycotted the city bus system.

episodes.title: Martin Luther King, Jr
episodes.description: Today we're going to learn about perhaps the best-known leader in the Civil Rights Era, Martin Luther King, Jr.

episodes.title: Student Civil Rights Activism
episodes.description: Today, we'll learn about the Little Rock Nine, the Greensboro Four, the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee, and the Freedom Riders.

episodes.title: Malcolm X and the Black Power Movement
episodes.description: Today, we’ll learn about Malcolm X’s origins, his work with the Nation of Islam, his break from that organization, and his eventual assassination.

episodes.title: The Black Panther Party
episodes.description: Explore the Black Panther Party and how a relatively small organization had a major influence on American history.

episodes.title: Women and the Black Power Movement
episodes.description: Today, we'll learn about how women contributed to several organizations, including the Black Panthers.

episodes.title: Marsha P Johnson and the Stonewall Rebellion
episodes.description: Today we’re learning about Marsha P. Johnson and the Stonewall rebellion.

episodes.title: War on Drugs
episodes.description: The War on Drugs is a decades-long United States policy intended to curb illegal drug use and trafficking.

episodes.title: Shirley Chisolm
episodes.description: Explore Shirley Chisholm’s political career, pioneering presidential campaign, and lasting legacy.

episodes.title: Jesse Jackson
episodes.description: Today, Clint Smith is teaching you about the Civil Rights activist and Icon, Reverend Jesse Jackson.

episodes.title: LA Uprisings
episodes.description: In this episode of Black American History, Clint Smith teaches you about the complicated history of racial tension in South Central Los Angeles.

episodes.title: Anita Hill and Clarence Thomas
episodes.description: Examine Clarence Thomas’s Supreme Court confirmation hearings, sexual harassment allegations, and the response within Black American communities.

episodes.title: Rap and Hip Hop
episodes.description: Explore rap and hip hop’s cultural significance through influential Black performers and groups.

episodes.title: Toni Morrison
episodes.description: Today, Clint Smith will teach you about the legendary writer Toni Morrison.

episodes.title: Hurricane Katrina
episodes.description: Examine Hurricane Katrina’s devastation, failures in disaster response, and the structural racism that intensified its impact on Black residents.

episodes.title: Barack Obama
episodes.description: In this episode, Clint Smith will explore the early life, political career, presidential campaign, and legislative milestones of Barack Obama.

episodes.title: Black Lives Matter
episodes.description: In the final episode of Crash Course Black American History, Clint Smith teaches you about the Black Lives Matter movement.
